Cloud Methodology.description: Cloud penetration testing methodology covering AWS, Azure, and GCP from external recon to full account compromise.

steps.task: Identify cloud provider — DNS records, response headers, WHOIS, Shodan
Enumerate S3/Azure Blob/GCS buckets — s3scanner, gcpbucketbrute
Search for leaked API keys/secrets — GitHub (truffleHog, gitleaks)
Check SSL certs for subdomain/service discovery — crt.sh
Identify cloud-hosted services — Shodan, Censys, FOFA
Azure tenant/domain enumeration — AADInternals, o365enum
AWS account ID enumeration via public S3 error messages
Test access with discovered API keys — validate scope and permissions
AWS — try unauthenticated S3 access: aws s3 ls s3://{bucket} --no-sign-request
Azure — device code phishing flow / MSOLSpray password spraying
GCP — test unauthenticated storage access: gsutil ls gs://{bucket}
Exploit SSRF to reach cloud metadata service (169.254.169.254)
Exploit overly permissive IAM roles on public-facing functions
AWS — enumerate-iam.py to identify all accessible permissions
AWS — list IAM users, roles, groups, policies
AWS — check for Secrets Manager and SSM Parameter Store secrets
Azure — AzureHound collection for all resources and roles
Azure — enumerate Key Vaults, storage accounts, VMs, service principals
GCP — enumerate IAM bindings, service accounts, secrets, GCS buckets
Identify overprivileged accounts (admin, owner, wildcard policies)
AWS — enumerate Lambda Function URLs (unauthenticated endpoints): aws lambda list-function-url-configs --function-name <fn>
AWS/Azure/GCP — enumerate AI/ML services: Bedrock models (aws bedrock list-foundation-models), Azure OpenAI (az cognitiveservices account list), Vertex AI (gcloud ai models list)
AWS — run Pacu iam__privesc_scan to identify escalation paths
AWS — attach AdministratorAccess policy to controlled user/role
AWS — assume-role into higher privilege role
AWS — Lambda code injection / environment variable override
Azure — abuse Managed Identity to get OAuth token from IMDS
Azure — app role assignment abuse for Global Admin escalation
GCP — service account key creation for persistence
GCP — update Cloud Function code with malicious handler
AWS — pivot via EC2 Instance Connect or SSM Session Manager
AWS — access cross-account roles via trust policy abuse
Azure — access other subscriptions via Managed Identity
GCP — impersonate other service accounts via token delegation
Steal credentials from cloud-native secrets stores
AWS — sync S3 buckets: aws s3 sync s3://{bucket} ./loot/
AWS — export RDS snapshots to attacker account
Azure — download blobs: az storage blob download-batch
GCP — download GCS objects: gsutil -m cp -r gs://{bucket} ./loot/
Extract database connection strings and dump databases
AWS — stop CloudTrail logging before sensitive operations
AWS — operate in regions without GuardDuty enabled
Azure — use Managed Identities instead of explicit credentials
GCP — use service account token to avoid direct user attribution
Minimize API call volume to avoid anomaly detection
AWS — GuardDuty evasion: create suppression filter (CreateFilter with ARCHIVE action) or add attacker IP to trusted IP set (CreateIPSet)
AWS — abuse Lambda Function URL with authType=NONE as covert C2 channel bypassing WAF/VPC controls: aws lambda create-function-url-config --auth-type NONE
Azure — disable Defender for Cloud alerts on subscription: az security auto-provisioning-setting update --name mma --auto-provision Off
AWS — create hidden IAM user with access keys, no console login tag
AWS — add attacker-controlled principal to role trust policy
Azure — add credentials to existing app/service principal (secret or certificate)
Azure — register federated credential linking to attacker OIDC issuer
GCP — create persistent service account key for offline authentication
GCP — add attacker account to org IAM policy with editor/owner role
Enumerate K8s cluster — kubectl get pods,secrets,cm,sa -A
Check service account permissions — kubectl auth can-i --list
Create privileged pod for node escape — mount /host and chroot
Read K8s secrets from etcd if accessible — etcdctl get / --prefix | grep -i password
Exploit misconfigured RBAC — create ClusterRoleBinding to cluster-admin
Compromise container registry (ACR/ECR/Artifact Registry) — inject malicious image layer
AI/ML services — test for prompt injection in Bedrock/Azure OpenAI deployed models; enumerate accessible RAG datastores (Kendra, AI Search indexes); check for exposed embeddings buckets
AWS SageMaker — enumerate public endpoints, notebook instances, and model artifacts in S3: aws sagemaker list-endpoints; check for unauthenticated inference endpoints
